origins: Families, sports, the military, workplaces, and some churches praise those who “keep it together.” Boys especially hear “Don’t cry.” We learn to bottle feelings, which then leak out as anger, numbness, or physical tension.
teaches: “Jesus wept.” Isaiah calls Him “a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.” Paul says, “Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.” David wrote, “I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping.” Paul also says, “when I am weak, then I am strong.” The Lord who is strongest shows emotion. Strength is not the absence of feeling. It is facing feeling honestly and bringing it to God and to safe people.
self_statements: I have to hold it together.
Showing emotion makes me a burden.
I will fall apart if I let it out.
errors: Believing I am either composed or weak.
Assuming people would think less of me.
Feeling vulnerable and concluding that it is dangerous.
questions: Who taught me that feelings are weakness?
What happens to the feelings I hold in?
Who is safe enough to share with?
What would a friend say to someone who felt this way?
What is one feeling I could name this week?
truth: Emotions are part of how God made me. Jesus wept, and strength includes honesty. I can name my feelings, bring them to God, and share them with safe people.
hw_truths: The Savior was acquainted with grief.
David poured out his tears to God.
Feelings are part of how God made me.
Safe people can help me carry them.
log: Each day, name one feeling and tell God about it.
actions: Release tension through a walk or slow breathing.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You wept. Teach me that strength includes honesty. Help me bring my feelings to You and to safe people. Amen.
hw_questions: What would I tell a friend?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Jesus wept, so my feelings are not weakness.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Strong people don't show emotion.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
